mike: Ran an nsys trace during a kvcache-heavy run on staging-dedicated. Batcher=8, eviction enabled. Seeing frequent H2D bursts every ~200ms coinciding with cache-eviction flushes. nvlink peer-copy kernels dominate the timeline. gist with full timeline: https://gist.github.com/redwood/abcdef :eyes:
tara: Can you paste the timeline snippet and the heavy kernel names? Also which alloc path (pinned vs pageable)?
mike: snippet below (trimmed):
````
Time(ms)  Event                               Duration(ms)
0.00     cudaMemcpyAsync H2D (pageable)        1.42
1.50     cuMemcpyPeerAsync (nvlink)           2.90
4.50     attention_fwd_kernel                 0.80
5.40     kvcache_read (host->device)          1.10
7.00     cuMemcpyPeerAsync (nvlink)           2.75
9.80     attention_fwd_kernel                 0.78

Notes: peer copy spikes align with batch flush points. nvlink utilization saturates for short bursts and we get pageable-stall warnings in the trace.
````
oliver: that looks like pageable host allocations. If we call cudaMemcpyAsync from pageable host memory, the driver creates a staging buffer and you get extra copies + CPU pinning under the hood -> high latency and pageable stalls. Are we using host-pinned allocs anywhere in the batcher path?
mike: not by default in dedicated staging. The allocator path uses std::vector + raw host ptrs from the request buffer (pageable). I toggled a local build to use cudaHostAlloc for the host buffer and re-ran: H2D peak drops ~6x, nvlink peercopy time drops by ~60%. quick repro command:
````
# profiling command (sanitized)
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt -o /tmp/nsys_kvcache --capture-range=cpuop --capture-range-end=none ./bin/infer --batcher=8 --kvcache-eviction=on --use-pinned-host=true

# runtime toggle in code (pseudo)
if (use_pinned_host) cudaHostAlloc(&ptr, size, cudaHostAllocPortable | cudaHostAllocMapped);
else ptr = malloc(size);
````
tara: perf-regression-bot just flagged commit abc123. The diff changed batching heuristic to immediate-flush-on-miss to reduce tail-latency for small requests. Seems that had the side-effect of creating many small H2D bursts. Reverting that change in a canary reduced H2D p99 for kvcache test back to baseline.
perf-regression-bot: alert: kvcache_h2d_p99 increased by 2.1x on master vs baseline after abc123. See CI artifact: https://ci.redwood/123/artifacts
oliver: short-term mitigations: (1) prefer a host-pinned buffer pool for kvcache transfers on dedicated nodes, (2) coalesce flushes in the batcher by allowing a 1-2ms aggregation window or soft-debounce on eviction-triggered flushes, (3) fall back to GPU staging when nvlink bandwidth is saturated. Longer term: update kernel selection logic to choose pipelined staging copy vs direct peercopy based on run-time nvlink BW probes. Also consider cudaMemPrefetchAsync for unified memory path.
mike: agreed. Action items: 1) add an nsys-based smoke test in CI that fails when H2D p99 for kvcache scenario exceeds threshold; 2) instrument batcher to tag flush reason (eviction vs timer vs forced); 3) implement pinned host buffer pool behind a flag and experiment with default-on for Dedicated. I'll upload full .qdrep and timeline slices to #eng-runtime-artifacts in a few mins. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: perf-alert: regression detected for kvcache workload (H2D p99 2.1x). Attaching perf diff summary. :warning:
